item.title: Users
item.description:
User Accounts 🔗

Anyone who uses Layer5 Cloud signs into a user account. Your user account is your identity on Layer5 Cloud and has a username and profile. For example, see Five’s profile.

Five - Platform Engineer

Organization: Orbital Labs
Role: User (Platform Engineer)
Plan: Team

Curious, enthusiastic, and reliably the first to discover that a feature works differently than the docs say it does.

item.title: Account Consolidation
item.description:
Layer5 Cloud recognizes one account per verified email address, no matter which method you use to sign in.

What changed 🔗

Previously, signing in with email/password, GitHub, or Google could each create a separate account, even when they shared the same email address. This led to a confusing experience: designs, organizations, and workspaces created under one sign-in method would appear to “disappear” when you signed in with another.

item.title: Set Notification Preferences
item.description:
Layer5 Cloud sends email when something happens that involves you: you earn a badge, your role changes, someone comments on your design. Notification preferences decide which of those emails reach you. Preferences belong to your account, so they apply in every organization you belong to.

Email is the only channel. Layer5 Cloud has no per-event choice between email and another channel.

Before you start 🔗

You need the View Profile permission, which the default user role holds. The preferences are on your own account, and you cannot set them for anyone else.

item.title: Manage Users
item.description:
The Users page is where administrators manage the people in an organization. It lists the organization’s members and carries the actions that put people into the organization, change what they can do, and take them out. This guide covers each action, who can run it, and what it changes.

To bring in people who do not have an account yet, or to let a group join without administrator action, use Invite Users. For what a user account is and how membership and roles combine, read the Users concept.

item.title: Invite Users
item.description:
An invitation is a link that lets people join one organization, with the roles and teams you choose, under limits you set: who may accept, how many may accept, when it stops working, and what accepting does. The same mechanism powers your organization’s open sign-up. This guide covers creating and managing invitations, what happens when someone accepts, and the separate direct invite for a single new person.

item.title: Review Access Requests
item.description:
An access request is a person asking for access to a Layer5 product capability, such as Kanvas. Layer5 Cloud collects these as signup requests in a queue. A Provider Admin reviews the queue, then approves or denies each request. Approval grants the requester Kanvas access and, for someone without an account, creates one.

This guide covers who can review requests, what the queue shows, and exactly what approval and denial do. It describes the queue that ships today. Layer5 Cloud has no general request flow for access to a specific design, workspace, or environment, and a denial does not restrict any resource. See What this does not cover.
